\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا} (muāinā karnā)}{معائنہ کرنا (muāinā karnā)}]{\ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا} (muāinā karnā) — to examine (a patient)}

\label{lesson:UR-C476-muaina-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for cancer, then the Urdu for afflicted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{muāinā karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to examine (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ڈاکٹر} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کا} \ur{معائنہ} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍākṭar ne marīz kā muāinā kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor examined the patient.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کا} \ur{معائنہ} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne bachche kā muāinā kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{muāinā karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{معائنہ}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muʿāyana}, \textquotedblleft{}looking at closely\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muāinā karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muāinā karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar ne marīz kā muāinā kiyā.} — The doctor examined the patient.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for cancer, then the Urdu for afflicted, then say \emph{muāinā karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{معائنہ} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To examine (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹیسٹ} (ṭesṭ)}{ٹیسٹ (ṭesṭ)}]{\ur{ٹیسٹ} (ṭesṭ) — a medical test}

\label{lesson:UR-C476-test}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for afflicted, then the Urdu for to examine.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹیسٹ}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹیسٹ}} — \emph{ṭesṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a medical test\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کل} \ur{میرے} \ur{خون} \ur{کا} \ur{ٹیسٹ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kal mere khūn kā ṭesṭ ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{ٹیسٹ}} (\emph{ṭesṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{test}.

Before the new one: say the Urdu for to examine, then the Urdu for a medical test.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حکیم} (hakīm)}{حکیم (hakīm)}]{\ur{حکیم} (hakīm) — a traditional physician}

\label{lesson:UR-C476-hakim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a medical test, then the Urdu for a diagnosis.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حکیم}}
\textbf{\ur{حکیم}} — \emph{hakīm} — \textquotedblleft{}a traditional physician\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادا} \ur{حکیم} \ur{کی} \ur{دوا} \ur{کھاتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā hakīm kī davā khāte haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather takes medicine from a traditional physician.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حکیم}} (\emph{hakīm}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥakīm}, \textquotedblleft{}a wise man\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu it is the healer of the old Greek and Arabic medicine.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بلوانا} (bulvānā)}{بلوانا (bulvānā)}]{\ur{بلوانا} (bulvānā) — to have (someone) sent for}

\label{lesson:UR-C476-bulvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a diagnosis, then the Urdu for a traditional physician.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بلوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{بلوانا}} — \emph{bulvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have (someone) sent for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{امی} \ur{نے} \ur{ڈاکٹر} \ur{کو} \ur{گھر} \ur{بلوایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ammī ne ḍākṭar ko ghar bulvāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mum had the doctor called to the house.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{حکیم} \ur{کو} \ur{بلوایا}, \emph{us ne hakīm ko bulvāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بلوانا}} (\emph{bulvānā}) is built on \textbf{\ur{بلانا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to call\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{bōll}, \textquotedblleft{}speak\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 9321): the form for having someone else do the calling.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a diagnosis, then the Urdu for a traditional physician, then say \emph{bulvānā} again
\end{itemize}
